newsitem.title: USA: Grand Casinos says Ojibwe assess contract.
newsitem.headline: Grand Casinos says Ojibwe assess contract.

text.p: Grand Casinos Inc said Wednesday that the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe plans to review whether it will renew its casino management contract with the company.
The Band's Corporate Commission owns two of Grand Casinos' four managed properties, Grand Casino Mille Lacs in Onamia, Minn., and Grand Casino Hinckley, in Hinckley, Minn.

The Band has created a task force to analyze the options available when its management agreements with Grand Casinos expire in April 1998 for the Grand Casino Mille Lacs and in May 1999 for the Grand Casino Hinckley.
Grand Casinos said the task force plans to complete an initial draft of its analysis this spring and present its final report to the Corporate Commission Board this fall.
Any decision by the Corporate Commission Board will be subject to approval by the Band Assembly and concurrence by Chief Executive, Marge Anderson.
"We are hopeful that we will have the opportunity to continue our partnership with the Band," said Lyle Berman, chairman of Grand Casinos, in a statement.
Grand Casinos owns and operates casinos and hotel resorts in Mississippi, Louisiana, and Minnesota.
